chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash from Abdillah ibn Sinan from a man from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) said:
When a man makes an oath upon his brother and he does not fulfill his oath, then upon the one who made the oath is the expiation for the oath.

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: His brother (or friend/companion in this context)
key_terms.اَلْمُقْسِمِ: The one who made the oath

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for an oath made upon another person that is not fulfilled?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *kaffarah* (expiation) in the context of mutual oaths, establishing that the burden of fulfillment or penalty rests on the initiator who compels the other party. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the validity of the oath itself and the obligation of the swearer, reinforcing the principle that one is accountable for their own verbal commitments even when used as leverage. The ruling underscores the seriousness of oaths in social contracts, ensuring that the party exerting pressure bears the religious consequence if the condition is not met.
